name: Chronobiology
citation: Aschoff, J. (1965). Circadian rhythms in man. Science, 148(3676), 1427-1432.

constructs.description: Self-sustaining biological clock in suprachiasmatic nucleus. Generates ~24h oscillation independent of environment, entrained by light via retinohypothalamic tract. Core mechanism of CB framework.
Time-dependent sensitivity to light pulses. Light advances phase in subjective evening, delays in subjective morning. Critical for circadian adaptation to seasonal and jet-lag perturbations.

Time-dependent modulation of behavioral and physiological responsiveness. SCN output gates activity levels, alertness, body temperature, and hormone secretion (melatonin, cortisol) across the 24h cycle.

rejection_rationale: IS the CB (Chronobiology) framework itself — circular reduction. SCN-mediated circadian rhythm mechanisms constitute the core of the CB framework. All chronobiological phenomena in the architectural domain are already addressed by CB as T1.

function_form.function_form: C(t) = A·sin(2π·t/τ + φ) + offset; τ ≈ 24.2h; φ = f(light_history)

variables.C(t): Circadian process output at time t
variables.\u03c6: Phase angle (entrained by light exposure pattern)

predictions: Alertness follows ~12h sinusoidal cycle, nadir at 2-4 AM
Bright light exposure (>1000 lux) phase-shifts circadian clock~1h/day
